title: How URL Filtering rule criteria combine

operator-expression.statement: A rule matches when this expression is true: Source IP Groups AND Source Countries AND URL Categories AND [Users OR/AND Groups OR/AND Departments] AND User Risk Profile AND [Location Groups OR Locations] AND Time AND Request Methods AND Protocols AND User Agent AND [Device Groups OR Devices] AND Device Trust.

quotes: Source IP Groups (AND) Source Countries (AND) URL Categories (AND) [Users (OR/AND) Groups (OR/AND) Departments] (AND) User Risk Profile (AND) [Location Groups (OR) Locations] (AND) Time (AND) Request Methods (AND) Protocols (AND) User Agent (AND) [Device Groups (OR) Devices] (AND) Device Trust.

unset-ignored.statement: An unset criterion is ignored, not treated as "matches nothing": a rule with no Locations applies at every location.

evidence.after: URL Categories: Select any number of URL super categories or categories or both.
quotes: Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.

url-categories2-and.statement: A second URL Categories field (`urlCategories2` in the API) is ANDed with the first: the URL must be in a category from each field, which makes the rule narrower, not broader.

quotes: The URL Categories fields are connected with a logical AND operator.
Note: The urlCategories and urlCategories2 parameters are connected with a logical AND operator

user-risk-score-levels.statement: The console's User Risk Profile criterion selects user risk score levels (by default Low 0–29, Medium 30–59, High 60–79, Critical 80–100; ranges are customizable through Support). The API carries it as `userRiskScoreLevels`.
user-risk-score-levels.conditions: The console-label-to-field mapping is a chain of evidence: the help describes the criterion as risk score levels, and the rule model's only risk field is userRiskScoreLevels.

quotes: User Risk Profile: Select the user risk score levels to which the rule applies.
Low: Level with user risk scores ranging from 0 to 29
Critical: Level with user risk scores ranging from 80 to 100

api-only-scoping.statement: The API also scopes rules by workload groups and by HTTP header profiles; these appear in tenant data even when operators never set them in the console.

quotes: // The list of preconfigured workload groups to which the policy must be applied.
// Name-ID pairs HTTP header profile to which the rule applies

payload-criteria-need-inspection.statement: Criteria that need the request itself (Request Methods, Protocols, URL path) can only be evaluated on decrypted traffic; on uninspected HTTPS only domain-level evaluation exists, so such rules silently do not fire.
payload-criteria-need-inspection.conditions: Chain of evidence: pre-decrypt evaluation sees only the destination domain.

quotes: During a CONNECT request or an incoming SSL connection (SNI), only the destination domain is available and not the full URL.

two-category-fields-and.note: The URL is only in the first field's category, so the AND fails and the rule does not match.
